entries.title: Durotar
body: A harsh land of red, cracked earth, crags and canyons on Kalimdor's eastern coast, cut off from the Barrens by the Southfury River. It is dry and hot, its plants are sparse, and its scorpids, boars, raptors and thunder lizards are hardy. The orcs see a harsh beauty in it: it reminds them of the red plains of their lost homeland, Draenor.

After the Battle of Mount Hyjal, Warchief Thrall led the orcs here, drove off the Razormane quilboar who held it, and with the help of the tauren founded a new homeland. He named it after his murdered father, Durotan. Its capital, Orgrimmar, lies in the north, and the land has become a home for the whole Horde, not least the Darkspear trolls of the southern coast.

entries.title: Valley of Trials
body: A valley in southern Durotar where young orcs and trolls are tested before they are counted as recruits of the Horde. By the time they leave its tall walls, they are ready for what waits beyond. Those who fail and die are left to bake in the desert sun.
The caves in the northern cliffs have lately filled with demons. They are weak, but their presence suggests the rumours are true: the Shadow Council has found a foothold in the land.

entries.title: The Den
body: A small cave carved out of the cliff in the middle of the Valley of Trials, fitted with the basic comforts of living. It is the starting camp for young orcs, and its trainers give them their first lessons.

entries.title: Burning Blade Coven
body: Caves in the red mountains on the northern edge of the Valley of Trials. Imps and other minor demons spill out of their mouth, and some say stronger demons inside have more than mischief in mind.
The cult of the Burning Blade, led here by the warlock Yarrog Baneshadow, has made the caverns its own.

entries.title: Razor Hill
body: An orcish town at the crossroads of central Durotar, where the roads run north to Orgrimmar, south to Sen'jin and west across the river to the Barrens. Its barracks are the largest building in town.

It was once just a hill. Soon after the Third War, the forces of Kul Tiras arranged a summit with Thrall here that was really an ambush. Rexxar went in the Warchief's place and killed the assassins. Today Gar'Thok commands the town, and Orgnil Soulscar hunts the Burning Blade from it.

entries.title: Sen'jin Village
body: A Darkspear fishing village of huts and a dock on Durotar's southern coast. Vol'jin moved his people here when they were driven from the Echo Isles, and named it after his father Sen'jin, who died saving his people from murlocs during the Third War.
Many of its people are herbalists and alchemists, and its witch doctors keep the loa close.

entries.title: The Echo Isles
body: A cluster of tropical islands off Durotar's south-eastern coast, teeming with raptors, lynxes and other predators. At the height of the Gurubashi Empire, the jungle trolls ruled from Stranglethorn all the way to these isles.

The Darkspears settled here after the Third War, but soon had to flee when Admiral Proudmoore's fleet attacked. When he was defeated, they returned, and had only a moment's peace before one of their own, the witch doctor Zalazane, betrayed them and drove them out again with his dark magic.

entries.title: Tiragarde Keep
body: A ruined Alliance stronghold on Durotar's eastern coast. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore built it hastily during his war on the orcs, and it fell when the Horde threw him back.

After the admiral's death, orders he had written before leaving Kul Tiras came to light. Lieutenant Benedict was sent with a reserve force to retake the keep and continue his crusade, and his men still hold the ruins, a stubborn thorn in the Horde's side.

entries.title: Kolkar Crag
body: A craggy gorge in southern Durotar, named for the Kolkar centaurs who hold it. Under Warlord Kolkanis they plot to attack the towns of Durotar: the Valley of Trials, Sen'jin, Razor Hill, even the gates of Orgrimmar.

entries.title: Thunder Ridge
body: A gorge south-west of Orgrimmar that was once an ancient forest, where trees grew in harmony with herds of thunder lizards under the watch of the spirit Owa'nohe.

Soon after Durotar was founded, a Kul Tiran lumber operation began cutting the forest and drove the lizards mad. Years later the Burning Blade razed what was left with demonic magic, to unsettle the region, and the lizards stampeded into Drygulch Ravine. Thrall asked Jaina Proudmoore's help to move them. The cultists still camp among the stumps.

entries.title: Skull Rock
body: A cave in north-eastern Durotar, one of the Burning Blade's holdouts in the region, led by the orc warlock Gazz'uz. It overlooks Bladefist Bay, named after Kargath Bladefist, the old chieftain of the Shattered Hand clan.

entries.title: Razorwind Canyon and Drygulch Ravine
body: Canyons on either side of the road between Razor Hill and Orgrimmar, nesting grounds of the Dustwind harpies. Drygulch Ravine, reached through a cave from the canyon, is where the stampeding thunder lizards ran when Thunder Ridge was razed.
The harpies have taken to banditry, robbing caravans and hoarding the loot on their cliffs, where their strongest guard the eggs.

entries.title: Southfury River
body: Probably Kalimdor's greatest river. It begins in a lake on Mount Hyjal, falls into the lands below in spectacular waterfalls, and runs south between Ashenvale and Azshara, then between the Barrens and Durotar, before emptying into the Great Sea near Ratchet. Three bridges cross it. Crocolisks hunt in its shallows.

entries.title: Scuttle Coast and Deadeye Shore
body: Durotar's eastern shore. The Scuttle Coast is littered with Kul Tiran ships smashed on the rocks in the great battles between the orcs and Admiral Proudmoore's fleet, and is a favourite spot for scavengers.
Deadeye Shore, to the north, is named after Kilrogg Deadeye, the orcish hero who led the Bleeding Hollow clan; a skull-shaped patch of sand missing one eye marks it.

entries.title: Spirit Rock and the Shrine of the Dormant Flame
body: Places sacred to the shaman of the Horde, in the mountains around the Valley of Trials. Spirit Rock, reached by the Hidden Path, is where young shaman drink a sapta to commune with the earth.

The Shrine of the Dormant Flame stands atop the tallest peak north-west of the valley, at the end of a secret spiral path. Shaman who have mastered fire light its brazier with the ember of a fire elemental they have defeated.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Shrine of the Dormant Flame

entries.title: Eitrigg
body: An aging orc warrior of the Blackrock clan, born on Draenor, and a veteran of the First and Second Wars. Warchief Blackhand named him one of his lieutenants alongside Orgrim Doomhammer and Varok Saurfang, and he served Doomhammer just as faithfully.

After the wars, in Lordaeron, he met a human paladin, Tirion Fordring, who spared him and was stripped of his title for defending an orc. The two old warriors came to respect each other and became friends despite everything between their peoples. Eitrigg now serves Thrall as a trusted adviser.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Eitrigg (introduction, The First and Second Wars)

entries.title: Gar'Thok
body: The orc commander of Razor Hill. In the first days of Durotar, his outpost was one of the orcs' first footholds in the land, and he still holds the crossroads against quilboar, centaurs, harpies and the humans of Tiragarde.

entries.title: Master Gadrin
body: A witch doctor of the Darkspear tribe at Sen'jin Village, and one of its keepers of lore. He knows the other troll tribes, and their magic, as well as any troll in Durotar.

entries.title: Zalazane
body: A Darkspear witch doctor and once Vol'jin's best friend. Old Sen'jin himself encouraged him to study witchcraft, and some Darkspears thought he was being groomed to lead the tribe one day. Both young trolls believed in Sen'jin's dream of a Darkspear homeland.

Zalazane betrayed it. On the Echo Isles he turned to dark voodoo, bent the minds of his own people into mindless thralls, and drove the rest of the tribe from their home. The Horde has tried to deal with him, and failed.

entries.title: Sen'jin
body: The late chieftain of the Darkspear tribe, a powerful witch doctor and spiritual leader. For years he led his people in peace on the remote Darkspear Islands. He saw the folly in other trolls' dreams of rebuilding their ancient empires, and dreamed instead of a home where the Darkspears could live free from fear, led by a shadow hunter as they had been long ago.
When Thrall's Horde came to his islands before the Third War, Sen'jin allied with them against the enemies threatening his people, and was killed. His son Vol'jin led the Darkspears into the Horde.

entries.title: Orgnil Soulscar
body: An orc of Razor Hill who has taken on the task of investigating the Burning Blade's activities in Durotar, and of rooting out the cultists before they can do more harm.

entries.title: The Burning Blade
body: The Burning Blade was once a clan of the old Horde, its warriors so drunk on demon blood they burned with fel fire. It survives as a cult of warlocks and fanatics who still serve the Burning Legion and answer to the Shadow Council.

About three years after Hyjal, the cult came to Durotar to tear down Thrall's peace. It razed Thunder Ridge with demonic magic, set its hidden cells in the caves and canyons of the land, and works to set the Horde and Theramore against each other. As Warchief Thrall's general and chief of security, Nazgrel's duty is to root them out.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Durotar (Cycle of Hatred, World of Warcraft)

entries.title: Proudmoore's War
body: Soon after Durotar was founded, a massive fleet from Kul Tiras arrived under Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore, a hero of the Second War and a staunch enemy of the orcs, determined to destroy Durotar before they could take root.

His daughter Jaina, lady of Theramore, chose to help Thrall rather than her father. Daelin died in the battle before she could reconcile with him or show him the orcs were no longer bloodthirsty monsters. In gratitude, the orcs let Jaina's forces return home in peace. Kul Tiras' wrecks still lie along the coast, and its last soldiers still hold Tiragarde.

entries.title: The Darkspear Pact
body: The Darkspears were once part of the Gurubashi Empire and suffered when it split into tribes, being smaller than the rest. They are mortal enemies of the Amani, and fought the Skullsplitters and Bloodscalps for years.

When Thrall led the Horde out of Lordaeron, his ships came to the Darkspears' islands and rescued them from the naga sea witch Zar'jira. The Darkspears owed the orcs a great debt, and allied themselves with the Horde in gratitude. Vol'jin has been one of Thrall's most trusted advisers ever since.
